headline: 1 Starknet class hash catalogued; 2 audit reports found; 0 deployed contract addresses verified on-chain — Starknet not in DeFiPunkd chainId support and Voyager rendered JS-only.

findings.text: D1: Starknet is not in the DeFiPunkd supported chainId list (1,10,56,130,137,324,8453,42161,43114,59144,81457,534352,11155111); Voyager block explorer at voyager.online returned a JS-only page with no renderable content. Web search for Extended Exchange Starknet contract addresses surfaced only generic contract stub pages on starkscan.co/voyager.online without Extended-specific name tags. No EVM bridge addresses were surfaced via D1 searches. All D1 results demoted to unknowns.

D2: The docs site at docs.extended.exchange was fetched successfully. The llms.txt index was walked in full. No dedicated 'Deployed Contracts' or 'Addresses' page was found in the index — neither a /docs/deployments, /docs/addresses, nor equivalent. The nearest candidate is the Technical Architecture page which references a Voyager class page (class hash 0x055ca2019a8677a996e7b583c5c9d0147d2854d0c477716af685e926ee4a5463) but not a deployed instance address. deployed_contracts_doc set to null.

D3: Smart Contract Audits page (docs.extended.exchange/extended-resources/more/smart-contract-audits.md) lists two audits: ChainSecurity at chainsecurity.com/security-audit/starkware-starknet-perpetual, and a Code4rena public competition report at code4rena.com/reports/2025-03-starknet-perpetual. The Code4rena report was fetched and confirms the repository github.com/starkware-libs/starknet-perpetual at commit 6103343c20bc797be598c04a10839bbdda073854. No in-scope deployed addresses (instance addresses) appear in the audit scope tables — only source file paths are listed.

D4: GitHub repository github.com/starkware-libs/starknet-perpetual was discovered from the Code4rena audit report (commit 6103343c20bc797be598c04a10839bbdda073854). This repo was not fetchable in this run (fetch quota exhausted). No Foundry broadcast artifacts, hardhat-deploy JSONs, or deployments.json were confirmed. Demoted to unknowns pending next run.

D5: Protocol.chains lists Starknet and Ethereum. Starknet: Voyager returned JS-only; no DeFiPunkd chainId support. Ethereum: web search and docs search surfaced no EVM bridge deposit contract addresses with confirmed Extended labelling. The API docs mention EVM deposits from Ethereum/Arbitrum/Base/BSC/Avalanche/Polygon but no contract addresses were found. All chains: zero addresses surfaced with on-chain evidence.
D6: No factory addresses were discovered in D1-D5, so D6 factory enumeration was not attempted.

D7: One candidate address-class artifact was found: Starknet class hash 0x055ca2019a8677a996e7b583c5c9d0147d2854d0c477716af685e926ee4a5463 from the Technical Architecture docs page. This is a class hash (Cairo class declaration), not a deployed instance address. Role taxonomy cannot be assigned without the deployed instance address. Recorded in unknowns.

D8: The Starknet class hash 0x055ca2019a8677a996e7b583c5c9d0147d2854d0c477716af685e926ee4a5463 was seen in a fetched doc page (not a block-explorer page), and no deployed instance address was confirmed. This entry remains in unknowns per D8 rules — not promoted to admin_addresses.

rationale.verdict: Discovery is incomplete: Starknet is outside DeFiPunkd chainId support and Voyager returned JS-only content, so no deployed instance addresses could be verified on-chain. The GitHub repo and two audit reports were located. Next run should fetch github.com/starkware-libs/starknet-perpetual for deployment artifacts, fetch the ChainSecurity PDF for in-scope addresses, and attempt Starkscan API or Voyager API for the deployed core contract address.

evidence.shows: Step 0 capability probe — website loads as a minimal SPA (React app), confirming web_fetch tool is functional.

D2: Official docs site confirmed at docs.extended.exchange. Overview page describes Extended as a perpetuals DEX built on Starknet by ex-Revolut team, using USDC collateral, offering 100+ markets with up to 100x leverage.

D2: Full documentation index. Confirms existence of Smart Contract Audits page, Bounty program page, Technical Architecture page, Vault page, and Deposits/Withdrawals page. No dedicated deployed-addresses page found in the index.

D3: Audit page listing ChainSecurity audit (chainsecurity.com/security-audit/starkware-starknet-perpetual) and Code4rena public competition (code4rena.com/reports/2025-03-starknet-perpetual). Confirms smart contracts are open source.

D7: Technical Architecture page references Starknet class hash 0x055ca2019a8677a996e7b583c5c9d0147d2854d0c477716af685e926ee4a5463 via a Voyager link as the deployed core contract class. Confirms all user funds are self-custodied in on-chain Starknet smart contracts. Architecture is a hybrid CLOB: off-chain matching, on-chain settlement via ZK proofs.

D3/D4: Code4rena audit report (published 2025-06-18) for Starknet Perpetual. Confirms source repository github.com/starkware-libs/starknet-perpetual at commit 6103343c20bc797be598c04a10839bbdda073854. Scope is 39 Cairo smart contracts, 3846 lines of Cairo code. No deployed instance addresses in scope table.

D5: Arbitrum, Base, BSC, Avalanche, Polygon EVM bridge contracts mentioned in API docs but no addresses found — not checked this run.
D7: Starknet class hash 0x055ca2019a8677a996e7b583c5c9d0147d2854d0c477716af685e926ee4a5463 is a Cairo class declaration, not a deployed instance address. Deployed core contract address unknown.

protocol_metadata.about: Extended is a perpetuals DEX built on Starknet by an ex-Revolut team, offering trading across 100+ crypto and TradFi markets (equities, FX, commodities, indices) with up to 100x leverage and USDC as base collateral. It operates as a hybrid CLOB: off-chain matching with on-chain settlement via Starknet ZK proofs, ensuring self-custody of user funds with every collateral-movement transaction subject to on-chain health checks. Users can deposit USDC from EVM chains (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, BSC, Avalanche, Polygon) via an integrated bridge, and a Community Vault allows users to deposit USDC to earn yield and receive XVS tokens usable as collateral.
